extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing creative writers seeking community classes, workshops, or short courses (adult community / continuing-education audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A community class catalog page listing short creative-writing courses and workshops; each entry states learning goals, pedagogical approach, intended student level, session count, dates, and format (online/in-person/asynchronous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fully Alive in the Moment: Writing with The Four Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: For those seeking a healing creative outlet. Writing will be our vehicle for self reflection, personal discovery, and processing lived experiences. We’ll write poems grounded in principles for living a life of integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags: cohort, personal growth. 4 Sessions. May 13 - June 3, 2026; 5:00-7:00 pm PT. Online. Listed under Fiction in catalog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldbuilding for All Genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to build richer story worlds on the page, whether you’re writing fiction or nonfiction. We’ll explore setting, culture, history, and environment and discover how deeply-realized worlds enhance everything that happens inside them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag: craft. 1 Session. May 16, 2026; 10:00-1:00 pm PT. In Person. Listed under Fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intro to Travel Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: This crash course will take you through the creative and business aspects of professional travel writing. We’ll cover research, the art of communicating a sense of place, pitching, and viable paths in the field. Leave with one or two draft pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags: generative, workshop, professional development. 2 Sessions. May 16 - May 30, 2026; 10:00-12:00 pm PT. Online. Nonfiction. Level: Intermediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleight of Hand for Writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore the seven principles of sleight of hand, then apply it to your writing! Perfect for new writers wanting to subvert, surprise, and delight their readers, and for writers looking to make writing feel like magic again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags: generative, craft. 2 Sessions. May 16 - May 23, 2026; 10:00-12:00 pm PT. Online. Fiction. Level: Intermediate. (Targets techniques for subversion, surprise, reader delight.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the Body
rubrics_metrics.description: Write from that which holds all our stories: the body. We’ll delve into personal history, identity, and the truths our flesh carries. You’ll read and study master writers exploring this topic and generate some writing of our own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags: generative, craft, close reading. 1 Session. May 30, 2026; 1:10-4:10 pm PT. Online. Listed under Fiction. (Emphasizes embodied writing, personal history, identity, close reading of master texts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Spellbound: Poetry as Alchemy
rubrics_metrics.description: Your strong emotions carry potent creative force. In this generative poetry workshop, you’ll explore language as invocation and spellwork, crafting charged work that channels rage, grief, longing, and more into powerful form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags: generative, personal growth. 1 Session. May 30, 2026; 10:00-1:00 pm PT. Online. Poetry. Status: Sold out (login/create account to receive notifications). (Focus on channeling strong emotions into formal/linguistic techniques.)

rubrics_metrics.name: In Answer to Another: Writing the “After” Poem
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to the poems that move you with poems of your own. We’ll read and analyze a dozen contemporary examples of the form. And you’ll gain tools for transforming homage, argument, and influence into original work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags: craft, close reading. 1 Session. June 6, 2026; 10:00-1:00 pm PT. Online. Poetry. (Emphasizes models, analysis of contemporary examples, and techniques for responding without copying.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Cataloging: Your Life in Lists
rubrics_metrics.description: A list is always more than just a list. We’ll explore what a list says about the list-maker, explore lists throughout history, and write our own. You’ll leave with new approaches to list-making as a tool for journaling and fueling creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags: generative, personal growth. 2 Sessions. June 6 - June 13, 2026; 10:00-12:00 pm PT. Online. Nonfiction. (Teaches list-based forms as creative and reflective tools; historical and practical approaches.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sliding Scale: Inspired By Images: Writing with Visual Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore the ways visual art can inspire new writing and infuse energy into existing projects. We'll take a field trip to the Frye Art Museum for inspiration and create and write from our own images, letting what we see guide our words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1 Session. June 6, 2026; 10:00-2:00 pm PT. In Person. Fiction. Level: Introductory. Notes: sliding-scale pricing; includes museum field trip and image-based generative exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer’s Welcome Kit (asynchronous)
rubrics_metrics.description: This asynchronous course features online workbooks, including ten essential templates in Word and Excel to kickstart your writing life, and resources professional writers use to get published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online Asynchronous. Fiction. Date listed as November 20, 2029 (ongoing/asynchronous product). (Provides practical templates and publishing resources rather than live workshop critique.)
